name: Swan District

climate: Few classic table-wine grapes keep their freshness in heat like this. It suits fortified wine, table grapes and raisins.
Chardonnay is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls in winter. Dry summers keep mildew and rot down, though young vines may need watering.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water.
soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Best for big crops of everyday wine, or table grapes.
